s2.key: af_heart|0.8|Every how-to video plays at the same speed, whether you keep up, or not.

s3a.key: af_heart|0.8|Falls are the second-leading cause of unintentional injury death worldwide.

s3b.key: af_heart|0.8|In one survey, three in four people didn't finish their home physical therapy exercises.

s3c.key: af_heart|0.8|And most cardiac arrests outside hospital happen at home, where nobody is checking your form.

s4a.key: af_heart|0.8|At least nine in ten deaf children are born to hearing parents.

s4b.key: af_heart|0.8|And a video can't see whether your hands are right.

s5.key: af_heart|0.8|In Step is the video that waits for you.

s6a.key: af_heart|0.8|Prop up your phone. It becomes the camera: an external camera, not the TV.

s6b.key: af_heart|0.8|Pose tracking runs in the phone's browser. Only body points travel to the TV, never video.

s7a.key: af_heart|0.8|At each key moment, the lesson pauses, and continues only when your pose is right.

s7b.key: af_heart|0.8|It counts your reps, times your balance, and if you're stuck, a coach gives one short, kind tip.

s8.key: af_heart|0.8|Safety comes first: no balance work until a chair is beside you. And if the camera drops, the lesson stops.

s9a.key: af_heart|0.8|The same engine teaches sign-language hand shapes, hand rehab, and CPR rhythm: practice only, not certification.

s9b.key: af_heart|0.8|Kids act out a story. And two people can practise together.

s10a.key: af_heart|0.8|A physiotherapist or teacher records a lesson once, on a phone.

s10b.key: af_heart|0.8|In Step finds the still moments, suggests the steps, and publishes it to the TV.

s11a.key: af_heart|0.8|Under the hood: an open lesson format, called dot eye step,

s11b.key: af_heart|0.8|one pure TypeScript gate engine, shared by the phone, the server, and the TV,

s11c.key: af_heart|0.8|and an open-source Vega player that any app can use.

s12.key: af_heart|0.8|In Step. The video that waits for you.
